description: The admission of a run (docs/design/orchestration-fable-5-2.md §14, « Un seul lieu d'écriture, imposé par l'hôte »): for each environment an installer may name in the marker of a runtime root, the free bytes, available to an unprivileged caller, that the filesystem of the root and the filesystem of the actual home of the account must each hold strictly above before a run starts. Floors are canonical positive decimal strings of bytes. They are initial operating choices of the reviewer of another provider, adopted by the maintainer on 19 November 2026; no measured safe threshold stands behind them. A floor decides whether work starts; passing it does not guarantee that the run finishes with space left.

workstation.basis: 32 GiB on the volume of the root, 16 GiB on the volume of the home. The development volume has room for a substantial reserve before another build or gate starts; the separate home reserve answers the disk that filled on 18 November 2026 and leaves the owner room to keep using the machine. Both floors passed on the workstation when they were chosen.
workstation.review: step 4: the peaks measured by repeated samples of free space during a step, a gate and two overlapping runs replace this operating choice

hosted-runner.basis: 4 GiB on the working filesystem, 2 GiB on the account filesystem. An ephemeral runner serves one job and protects no interactive workstation; the account filesystem is protected independently when it is separate. Assumed, not verified: both pinned images exceed these figures at each admission, after host packages and dependencies are installed; the first CI run that admits through the entry verifies it.
hosted-runner.review: step 4: the peaks measured by repeated samples of free space during a step, a gate and two overlapping runs replace this operating choice

server.basis: 64 GiB on the volume of the root, 16 GiB on the volume of the home. A provisioning assumption of a persistent host with several sessions: twice the working-volume reserve of the workstation, and its account-volume reserve. The multiplier is an operating choice; no server observation nor measured concurrency factor stands behind it.
server.review: step 4: the peaks measured by repeated samples of free space during a step, a gate and two overlapping runs replace this operating choice
